subject: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T15:12:00Z
Subject: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered:
- Goals: low-latency reranking for search (embedding -> reranker pipeline), structured outputs for downstream workflows, and predictable p99 latency for interactive sessions.
- Architecture note: you plan to route request traffic through your API gateway to Redwood Hosted endpoints; you also want the option for Private (VPC) later.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) FinLytics: share a small sample of the request payloads (anonymized) and the largest embedding batch sizes you expect.
2) Redwood: provide SDK quickstart + sample auth flow and a short repro test for the 5xx you saw in staging. I've attached the SDK snippet and a repro checklist.
3) Schedule technical sync (30m) next week with Camila (integration PM) and Dev (backend) to walk the SDK/auth and routing patterns.

Urgent item: you mentioned intermittent 5xx errors during a quick smoke test yesterday. If you can forward the request ids or attach the stack traces, our infra team can prioritize repro. For speed, please include the exact request payload and the timestamp (UTC).

I've attached: repro_steps_postcall.md (lightweight checklist) and sdk-auth-sample-code.zip.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this week to pair on the repro.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro

Thanks Marissa — good write-up. Attaching a small log snippet and the exact payload that tripped the 502/503 in our staging cluster. The failures happened between 2026-08-05T14:42:10Z and 2026-08-05T14:44:05Z from our side.

What we attached: finlytics_5xx_log_snippet.txt (contains request id FL-req-5591 and the upstream nginx 502 response), and a JSON file with the exact payload (removed PII). We also included the stack trace where our gateway shows Redwood responded with 502 a few times.

We tried two variants:
- Single request with embedding batch of 32, payload ~ 120KB
- Single request with batch of 128, payload ~ 480KB (higher timeout risk)

Would love for Dev/Camila to look at this and advise whether we should tune timeouts or reduce payload chunking for now. Also curious whether structured output/tool-calling (we plan to use your tool calling for entity enrichment) could increase latency.

Alex

On Wed, Aug 5, 2026 at 15:12, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: ...
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T20:45:00Z
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro

Hi Alex — Camila here (PM on Integrations). Thanks for the logs and the payloads — very helpful. Quick read: the 502s line up with sustained payloads > ~300KB and embedding batch sizes >= 64. A few things to check on your side while we dig in: 

1) Client-side timeouts: make sure your gateway is configured with a higher upstream timeout for long-running reranks (we recommend 60s p99 target for large batches).
2) Payload chunking: if you can break the batch into smaller sub-batches (e.g., 32) and merge/rerank client-side, that will reduce peak memory and latency at the Redwood endpoint.
3) Retry/backoff: use exponential backoff on 5xxs with jitter — don't retry immediately in tight loops.

From our side, Dev/Neha will attempt to repro in a staging environment with the same payloads and will capture logs. I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow (calendar invite to follow).

For transparency, here's our short repro plan:
- Replay the payloads through our hosted staging endpoint (same model variant you were using).
- Toggle continuous batching off to isolate request behavior.
- Instrument timeouts and collect kernel-level logs if we see OOMs or unexpected terminations.

I'll follow up with an invite and a preliminary timeline.

—Camila
Camila Reyes | Product Manager, Integrations
camila.reyes@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T02:10:00Z
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro

Thanks — I've started the repro using the 480KB payload you attached (batch=128). Initial findings: when continuous batching is enabled and multiple concurrent requests hit the same shard, memory pressure leads to transient worker restarts that manifest as 502s from the gateway.

Immediate mitigation I recommend for staging and prod rollout:
- Set client upstream timeout to 60s.
- Start with embedding batch <= 32 for live traffic; we can increase once autoscaling validation is complete.
- On Redwood side, we'll pin a model variant with conservative KV cache limits and disable aggressive continuous batching for the FinLytics route until we confirm safe memory profiles.

Attached a short log extract I pulled: finlytics_5xx_log_snippet.txt. Next steps for us:
1) I will run a controlled load test with batches [8, 32, 64] and report p50/p95/p99.
2) Neha will instrument an embedding size limiter in the SDK to warn at client-side.

Alex — would you be able to enable a staging route that sends traffic from a single machine (so we remove cross-shard contention) for our repro? That will speed root-cause identification.

—Dev
Senior Backend Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T07:18:00Z
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro

Thanks Dev — we can do that. I've asked ops to stand up a staging route that pins traffic to a single origin at 2026-08-06T09:30Z UTC. We'll keep payload at batch=128 for the first run so you can reproduce the behavior; after that we'll try reduced batch sizes.

One quick question for the SDK/auth flow: our gateway currently sends a short-lived JWT to Redwood and rotates it every 5 minutes. Is that rotation frequency OK or will it cause auth failures under load? We're happy to switch to a 15-min lifetime if that's better.

Alex
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call next steps + 5xx repro

Hi Alex — quick note on auth: short-lived JWTs are fine as long as your gateway can attach the token to the request without extra round trips to auth servers on the hot path. A 5-minute lifetime is OK; rotating to 15 minutes adds safety but is not required. We'll also add a client-side SDK warning when the token is within 30s of expiry to avoid mid-request failures.

Operational next steps:
- Dev will run the controlled load at 09:30 UTC and share p50/p95/p99.
- Camila will send the calendar invite for the 30-min follow-up to review logs and plan the rollout.
- Marissa will update the HubSpot record with the recommended starting configuration (batch=32, timeout=60s, token life 5m).

If we confirm worker restarts on our staging repro, we'll propose a temporary route-level throttling and an autoscale window to avoid impacting production.

—Neha
Applied ML / Infra
